topic: High-Level Synthesis with Game Theoretic Scheduling

entries.objective: M5 required converting my M1-M4 bullet structures into flowing academic prose for the Introduction and Background sections. I had all the technical content but needed the transition sentences to connect the power motivation, prior methods, and the game-theoretic proposal into a coherent narrative.
entries.prompt: I have these three ideas for the introduction: (1) power is important in VLSI because of battery life and heating; (2) HLS has three steps: scheduling, allocation, binding, and poor scheduling wastes power; (3) existing ILP and LP methods are complex and do not handle scheduling and binding together. Connect these into an introduction paragraph that leads to the game theory proposal.
entries.ai_output_summary: Claude wrote a paragraph that opened with the power motivation (battery life, reliability, 50%/10C rule), moved to HLS and its three steps, then identified the gap in existing methods (separate treatment of scheduling and binding), and ended with a sentence introducing the game-theoretic approach. The structure followed my three points exactly.

actions: Checked every factual claim in the generated paragraph: 50%/10C rule confirmed in Small [3]; HLS three steps confirmed in Gajski [5] and Benini [4]; ILP/LP limitation confirmed in Shiue and Chakrabarti [2]. The game-theoretic proposal is from Murugavel and Ranganathan [1]. All content matches the references.

entries.reflection: All three ideas and all the supporting facts were mine from M1. The AI helped connect them into a paragraph with smooth transitions. I rewrote the final version in my own words after using the AI output as a structural guide.

entries.objective: The methodology section (Section III) needed to present the game model, auction type selection, and three power-reduction techniques as separate subsections. I had the content from M1 but was unsure how to divide it into IEEE subsection headings that flow logically.
entries.prompt: My methodology covers: (A) the key idea that FUs are players bidding power cost, Nash decides; (B) why I chose first-price sealed-bid over English, Dutch, and second-price; (C) three power-reduction techniques: FU sharing, path balancing, register assignment; (D) the cost function equations. Suggest four subsection headings in IEEE style that present these in logical order.
entries.ai_output_summary: Claude suggested: 'A. Modeling the Problem as a Game', 'B. Auction Type Selection', 'C. Power-Reduction Techniques', 'D. Cost Function and Optimal Assignment'. The order matched my content grouping. It added no new content suggestions.

actions: Compared the proposed headings against the structure of Murugavel and Ranganathan (2003). The paper's sections III-V cover the same topics in a similar order (game model, cost function, techniques). The subsection heading style follows IEEE conference paper conventions.
